ticket.title: the unified workspace index and the root store index are the same sqlite file, so each command truncates the other view
ticket.description:
Found 2026-11-10 while chasing why the benchwork panel showed 7 InProgress tickets.  THE SYMPTOM THAT NOTICED IT. The unified index held 7 InProgress rows; after a failed reap it held 169 rows instead of 365 - every member ticket gone from the panel. Nothing was lost on disk, but the view collapsed to one store.  THE CAUSE. StorypoleWorkspaceStore::open uses the ROOT STORE sqlite path for the unified index (workspace/store.rs, `open_and_sync_index(&rs.sqlite_path(), ...)`), while StorypoleStore::open rebuilds that same file from the root store ledger alone. So one file backs two different scopes and the last command to run decides which view it holds:  `storypole list` (root store)        -> 169 rows, harness tickets only  `storypole ledger-reconcile` (workspace) -> 365 rows, every store  Neither is wrong on its own; the file is the thing that cannot hold both. A panel reads whatever the previous command left, so it can show a partial board or a full one depending on unrelated activity, and a crash in the middle of a workspace sync leaves the partial view in place - which is exactly what was observed.  SUGGESTED SHAPE. Give the unified index its own file (e.g. `.gaugeblock/storypole/workspace.sqlite`) so a store-scoped command cannot truncate a suite view, or make the two scopes share one builder that always unions every store. Until then: run a workspace-scoped command (ledger-reconcile) after per-store work, and do not read the row count as evidence about the suite without knowing which command wrote it.

FIXED 2026-11-10 — the suite view has its own file, and stale indices rebuild once.

THE CHANGE. `StorypoleWorkspaceStore` no longer borrows the root store's `index.sqlite`. It opens
`<store>/workspace.sqlite` through a new `index::open_index`, which creates the schema and inserts nothing - the unified
view is filled by `sync_all_members`, which already rebuilds from every store in one transaction. The root store keeps
its own `index.sqlite` and its own store-only view.

WHY A SEPARATE ENTRY POINT RATHER THAN A PATH CHANGE. `open_and_sync_index` rebuilds an index from ONE ledger, and
pointing it at the workspace file would have rebuilt the suite view from the root ledger - the bug, moved. The two
openers now say what they mean: one seeds from a ledger, the other waits to be filled.

A SECOND DEFECT SURFACED WHILE FIXING THIS, and it is the reason the symptom was worse than "two views fight".
Rebuilds are gated on `(ledger_len, ledger_mtime, replay_version)`, and a file written by the workspace has a meta row
saying it is current for the root ledger too - the ledger had not changed, so the store trusted the file and kept serving
STALE MEMBER ROWS in a root-scoped query. Measured after splitting the files: `storypole list --include-archived` at the
root still printed 196 member keys. Nothing in the ledger would ever invalidate that, so `REPLAY_VERSION` went 2 -> 3:
the only signal available for "these rows were written under different rules, rebuild them".

MEASURED AFTER THE FIX, on this suite:
  STORE-SCOPED list --include-archived    -> 172 rows, zero member keys
  suite-scoped ledger-reconcile           -> 368 rows, 0 in_progress
  and the order no longer matters: running the store-scoped command left the suite view at 368 instead of truncating it
  to 172, which is what the board needed all along.

TESTS. `workspace_index_isolation_tests`: a suite view of two stores survives a store-scoped open (the old behaviour
truncated it to the one row the root ledger holds), and the two scopes write different files.

NOT DONE. The stale `index.sqlite` files from before the bump are rebuilt on next open rather than deleted, so a checkout
that never runs a store-scoped command keeps its old file harmlessly. No migration is required.

ALREADY DONE, verified 2026-11-10: the suite view has its own file. .gaugeblock/storypole/index.sqlite and .gaugeblock/storypole/workspace.sqlite are distinct inodes (57423345 and 57423359), so a store-scoped command can no longer truncate the suite view; the fix landed as 3b38f1e and GB-355 closed its remaining half - foreign rows being purged on open and list routing through the rollup.
